items.title: Fix PR feed-validation for the DB-first contract (#124)
items.description: A PR that adds a scraper can pass CI again. The validation script still demands a matching --output line in the nightly workflow -- a line the DB-first model no longer has -- so every new-scraper PR fails for a reason that is now false. Replace that rule: a scraper pending entry is valid when its command begins `python scrapers/` (or `python scripts/`) and its output is cities/<city>/<name>.ics, i.e. it satisfies the feeds table insert-time trigger contract. Fold in the spurious-failure false positive so the script reports only real problems. Done when: a branch adding only a scraper's pending-feeds entry (no workflow edit) validates clean; a pending entry violating the DB trigger contract is flagged with a useful message; an ICS-URL-only entry still validates self-contained; malformed entries are still rejected; make lint and make test pass. No blockers.
items.notes: Rewrote scripts/validate_pr_feeds.py for the DB-first model. Removed WORKFLOW_PATH/get_workflow_scraper_outputs, the pending-entry 'must have a matching --output workflow line' check, and the new-scraper 'must be referenced in the workflow' check (the spurious-failure false positive: the DB-first runner executes active feeds-table rows, so generate-calendar.yml carries no per-scraper lines). Added SCRAPER_OUTPUT_RE / SCRAPER_CMD_RE mirroring the validate_scraper_row() trigger in supabase/ddl/16_feeds.sql; each scraper pending entry is now checked for a command beginning 'python scrapers/' or 'python scripts/', an output matching '^cities/[a-z0-9-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.ics$', and existence of the referenced .py. ICS-URL entries stay self-contained; ics_url entries skip all scraper checks. Removed the workflow from is_relevant (a workflow-only PR is no longer a feed-registration change). Decision (unattended, pre-approved): interpreted 'fold in the spurious-failure false positive' as the stale new-scraper-workflow-reference check, since both workflow dependencies are the only remaining false failures. Added tests/test_validate_pr_feeds.py (10 tests) at the validate() seam with get_changed_file_statuses + ROOT monkeypatched: DB-first new-scraper PR validates clean with no workflow edit, command/output contract violations flagged with useful messages, missing cmd flagged, missing .py flagged, ICS-URL self-contained, new scraper without any entry flagged, feeds.txt registration passes, relevance. Checks: make lint clean (ruff/pyright/ty/pyrefly/zuban + JS), make test green (108 pytest + 211 vitest). No blockers remain.

items.title: Emit X-SOURCE-URL from the base scraper (#124)
items.description: The base scraper gains an optional source_url class attribute. When a subclass sets it, every emitted VEVENT carries X-SOURCE-URL with that value; when it is unset (None), output is unchanged. The JSON stage already reads X-SOURCE-URL, so a scraper can point at its source page without special-casing. Done when: a subclass with source_url set produces VEVENTs carrying X-SOURCE-URL; a subclass without it produces output identical to today (no new header); the behavior is asserted at the scraper's calendar seam; make lint and make test pass. No blockers.
items.notes: Added `source_url: str | None = None` class attribute to BaseScraper and emit `event.add("x-source-url", self.source_url)` in create_event(), guarded by truthiness so unset subclasses are byte-for-byte unchanged. Test seam: create_calendar() -> to_ical() (the scraper's calendar output), tests/test_base_scraper.py (2 tests): a subclass with source_url set yields `X-SOURCE-URL:<value>` on the VEVENT; a subclass without it emits no X-SOURCE-URL header (red before the change). This is the fallback event URL the JSON stage already reads (scripts/ics_to_json.py:336), so the item-3 scraper can point at its CVB source page with no JSON special-casing. Checks: make lint clean (ruff/pyright/ty/pyrefly/zuban + JS), make test green (110 pytest + 211 vitest). No blockers. Decision (unattended, pre-approved): no new abstraction added; a plain optional class attribute was the smallest change satisfying current pressure.

items.title: Visit Bloomington scraper: full API pull and timed single events (#124)
items.description: A new dedicated Visit Bloomington scraper pulls the CVB's whole inventory over the CMS's same-origin REST API and emits calendar-ready events. It fetches the token once per run, pages the events endpoint to exhaustion (limit at most 50; skip advanced until skip + limit >= count; an explicit sort), spaces requests to respect the site's Crawl-delay: 2, and sends a realistic desktop-Chrome user agent (Akamai 403s the default requests UA). Per event: recid becomes a stable UID; clock times are kept wherever the source has startTime/endTime (all-day only when it genuinely has none); location comes from the source's GeoJSON coordinates; description is the API HTML stripped to plain text with no length cap; the event URL is the CVB event page. Only events with an occurrence inside the Horizon are emitted -- the source is pulled in full and filtered client-side on the date field, never with a server-side start-date bound or the date_range filter. The scraper subclasses the base scraper and hardcodes name, domain and timezone (America/Indiana/Indianapolis), so it needs no --name. Done when: fetch_events() returns one event per non-recurring occurrence inside the Horizon with clock times where the source has them; paging continues until the reported count is exhausted with the browser UA and crawl-delay spacing; a mocked payload yields the expected UID shape, coordinates-to-location, untruncated stripped description, CVB event URL, and source URL header; a non-200 response is surfaced, not silently swallowed; no workflow, Node, browser, or new dependency is required; tests mock HTTP at the fetch_events() seam with captured sample payloads; make lint and make test pass. Blocked by: item 2 (base source_url).
items.notes: Built scrapers/visit_bloomington.py (BaseScraper subclass, Pattern A: hardcoded name/domain/timezone, no --name). Fetches the token once from /plugins/core/get_simple_token/, then pages /includes/rest_v2/plugins_events_events_by_date/find/ with filter:{} and explicit sort, limit=50 (Akamai 403s >=64), skip steps until skip+limit>=count, MAX_PAGES=60 cap, 2s Crawl-delay spacing, desktop-Chrome UA. Maps each doc: UID=md5(recid-occurrenceDate)@visitbloomington.com (stable across title edits, unique per occurrence); location built from location/address1/city/state/zip; geo from loc.coordinates GeoJSON [lng,lat] -> (lat,lng); description = API HTML stripped to plain text with no length cap; url = CVB event page /event/<slug>/<recid>/ (slug from title; never linkUrl/origin). startTime/endTime -> timed DTSTART/DTEND; genuine all-day (no startTime) -> DATE + exclusive DTEND; startTime without endTime -> +1h default. Non-200 surfaces as RuntimeError. Horizon: full pull then client-side filter on `date` in city tz. BaseScraper.create_event now emits GEO when data['geo'] is present (small generic addition; inert for existing scrapers), asserted at test_base_scraper.py. Decision (unattended, pre-approved): item 3 emits single/non-recurring events only (recurType==0) — matching the ticket title 'timed single events'; the API already pre-expands recurrence into per-occurrence docs, so recurring expansion (incl. collapsing a daily multi-day festival into one span) is item 4's deliverable. Tests: tests/test_visit_bloomington.py (23 tests) mocks requests.get at the fetch_events() HTTP seam against captured payloads in tests/fixtures/bloomington/visit_bloomington_events.json (4 single-event docs + 1 recurring doc). Live run 2026-09-16: 1663 occurrence docs, 159 single events emitted (correct times, GEO, CVB URL, X-SOURCE/X-SOURCE-URL, untruncated description). Checks: make lint clean (ruff/pyright/ty/pyrefly/zuban + JS), make test green (133 pytest + 211 vitest). No blockers. Next: item 4 (recurrence).

items.title: Expand recurring series into individual occurrences (#124)
items.description: A recurring Visit Bloomington series (a weekly trivia night, a monthly program) appears once per occurrence inside the Horizon, each with its own date and time, instead of collapsing into a single wide block or being dropped. Occurrence identity is stable across edits and unique per date: a hash of the source recid plus the occurrence date. A genuinely multi-day event (a Friday-Sunday festival) stays one span with an exclusive end date. Expansion uses the source's own recurrence fields, not a naive start-date past-gate. Done when: a mocked recurring payload yields one event per occurrence inside the Horizon and none outside it; two occurrences of the same series have distinct UIDs and editing the title does not change a UID; a genuinely multi-day event emits a single span with an exclusive end date; tests cover weekly and multi-day cases at the fetch_events() seam; make lint and make test pass. Blocked by: item 3 (the scraper).
items.notes: Classified each API document on the source's own `recurrence` field: a non-empty recurrence string marks a recurring-series occurrence (live site: recurType 1/3/4/5/7, all carrying `recurrence`), emitted as one event keyed on its `date`; documents with no recurrence (recurType 0 single, recurType 99 ongoing/multi-day) are the event itself. Removed the old `recurType != SINGLE_RECUR_TYPE` skip. `_parse_doc` now dispatches to `_single_day_event` (unchanged single-day mapping) or `_multi_day_event`, both sharing a new `_event` builder. Multi-day: all-day span -> DTSTART = local start date, DTEND = local end date + 1 day (exclusive); timed span uses start/end clock times. UID stays md5(recid-occurrenceDate)@visitbloomington.com: stable across title edits, unique per occurrence, and for a multi-day span keyed on the span's first day so the source's per-day documents collapse. fetch_events() dedupes by UID (the source emits one document per day of a multi-day span). Horizon: recurring occurrences filtered on `date`; non-recurring spans kept when they overlap [today, horizon]. Tests: added TestRecurringExpansion (weekly per-occurrence incl. one beyond the Horizon, distinct UIDs, title-edit stability) and TestMultiDayEvents (single exclusive-end span; per-day documents collapse) at the fetch_events() seam, and updated TestSingleEventMapping to drop the now-false 'skips recurring' assertion. Decision (unattended, pre-approved): keyed classification on `recurrence` rather than hardcoding recurType values, because a live 1663-doc pull showed recurrence types 1/3/4/5/7 always carry the field and multi-day type 99 never does, so the field is the source's own semantic signal. Live run 2026-09-16: 1663 occurrence docs -> 808 events (was 159 single-only); Downtown Shop Night emitted 2 in-horizon occurrences with distinct UIDs; Heist collapsed to one 2026-09-03..2026-09-21 span; no duplicate UIDs. Checks: make lint clean (ruff/pyright/ty/pyrefly/zuban + JS), make test green (139 pytest + 211 vitest). No blockers.

items.title: Prefilter Visit Bloomington events to the city's allowed towns (#124)
items.description: Volume control at scrape time. Events whose location falls outside Bloomington's allowed-town list are dropped before they reach the ICS, while nearby in-scope towns (Nashville, Spencer, Martinsville, Ellettsville, Brown County) keep their events. The existing authoritative combine-time geo filter is untouched -- the scrape-time prefilter is an optimization, not a replacement, and the scope is the existing allowlist, not Bloomington-only. Done when: out-of-area events are absent from the emitted set and in-scope towns are present; the prefilter uses the existing allowlist, not a Bloomington-only bound; the combine-time geo filter is unchanged; make lint and make test pass. Blocked by: item 3 (the scraper).
items.notes: Added a scrape-time geo prefilter in scrapers/visit_bloomington.py.fetch_events(). It loads Bloomington's allowed-town allowlist from the SAME source of truth the combine-time filter uses: load_allowed_cities(str(CITY_DIR)) + location_matches_allowed_cities() imported from scripts/combine_ics (CITY_DIR = <repo>/cities/bloomington, whose city.conf lists all 17 allowed towns incl. Nashville/Spencer/Martinsville/Ellettsville). Reusing the shared helpers guarantees the prefilter matches the authoritative filter's semantics exactly (allowlist substring match, virtual/venue-only passthrough, excluded-city handling) and is not a Bloomington-only bound. Each parsed event is checked after the horizon/dedupe guards; out-of-area events are dropped before reaching the ICS and the run logs the count ('... N dropped outside the allowed towns'). combine_ics.py is untouched. Tests: tests/test_visit_bloomington.py::TestGeoPrefilter (3 tests) at the fetch_events() seam -- an Indianapolis-address event is absent, a Nashville (in-scope surrounding town) event is present, and a venue-only location with no address indicator passes through (the optimization must not over-filter). Added _located_single_doc helper. Decision (unattended, pre-approved): imported the existing combine_ics helpers rather than reimplementing the allowlist logic, so there is one geo-filter definition, not two. Live run 2026-09-16: 1663 occurrence docs -> 804 events, 6 docs (2 distinct out-of-area events: 'McGlocklin Park, Market Street, IN 47464' and "Sleeper's Bar, ... 47404" -- both address strings naming no allowed town, so the combine-time filter drops them too) were filtered; in-scope Bloomington/Nashville locations retained. Checks: make lint clean (ruff/pyright/ty/pyrefly/zuban + JS), make test green (142 pytest + 211 vitest). No blockers.

items.title: Harden the fetch and make coverage degradation visible (#124)
items.description: The scraper survives the source's anti-bot behavior and reports a silent coverage drop rather than hiding it. On a burst of 403s it re-fetches the token and retries once; requests stay spaced to respect the documented crawl delay and page limit. Each run logs occurrences fetched and events emitted, and a fetch below 50% of the trailing 7-run median is treated as a warning. No new alerting system -- the existing nightly failure signal remains the alarm. Done when: a 403 burst triggers a single token re-fetch and one retry and a successful retry is not treated as failure; requests stay spaced per the crawl delay and within the page limit; the run reports occurrences fetched and events emitted; a fetch below half the trailing 7-run median logs a warning; tests cover the non-200 / retry path at the fetch_events() seam; make lint and make test pass. Blocked by: item 3 (the scraper).
items.notes: Hardened scrapers/visit_bloomington.py. (1) 403 retry: split the request primitive into _request (raw GET) + _get (raising, token path) and added _fetch_page, which on an events-endpoint 403 re-fetches the token (via _fetch_token), waits CRAWL_DELAY, and retries the same page exactly once; a second 403 raises RuntimeError so failure still surfaces. A class attribute _token_refreshed, reset per run in fetch_events(), bounds re-fetching to one per run; _fetch_page threads the (possibly refreshed) token back to _fetch_docs for later pages. A successful retry continues to map the full page, not treated as failure. (2) Spacing/page limit unchanged: inter-page time.sleep(CRAWL_DELAY), PAGE_LIMIT=50 (< Akamai's 64 403 threshold), MAX_PAGES=60 bound; retry also waits CRAWL_DELAY. (3) Run telemetry: the existing info line reports extracted occurrences fetched and events emitted (plus out-of-area drops). (4) Silent-degradation guard: each run appends {date, fetched, emitted} to report/<city>/visit_bloomington.runs.json (capped RUN_HISTORY_MAX=30), and _warn_if_degraded logs a warning when fetched < DEGRADATION_FRACTION (0.5) * _trailing_median of the last RUN_HISTORY_WINDOW=7 prior fetched counts; no new alerting system. Decision (unattended, pre-approved): persisted the run history inside report/<city>/ because the workflow already commits that path wholesale (git add report/), so the guard persists across nightly CI runs with NO workflow edit (item 7's no-workflow-change criterion stays true); the history write is non-fatal (logs a warning on OSError) so a read-only checkout cannot break the scrape. Tests: TestFetchRetry (2) and TestDegradationGuard (3) added at the fetch_events() seam, plus an autouse fixture redirecting RUN_HISTORY_PATH to tmp_path so no test writes into the repo. Checks: make lint clean (ruff/pyright/ty/pyrefly/zuban + JS), make test green (147 pytest + 211 vitest). No blockers. Risk noted: the retry path is covered only by mocked HTTP (not reproducible live).

items.title: Register Visit Bloomington as a primary Bloomington source (#124)
items.description: The source lands in the pipeline through the standard DB-first registration path, with no workflow edit. Registering with the display name exactly `Visit Bloomington` writes the pending-feeds entry whose command begins `python scrapers/` and whose output is the Bloomington ICS path -- satisfying the feeds table's insert-time trigger -- and the nightly pending-feeds processor inserts the active DB row with no manual write. The source is deliberately not added to the aggregator list, so it ranks as a primary source, wins dedup over the Limestone Post echo, and shared events merge to `Visit Bloomington, Limestone Post`. Update the Bloomington sources checklist to move the source to implemented and record the concrete sitemap fallback trigger (contingency only, triggered by three consecutive non-200 nightly runs after an in-run token re-fetch and retry, or a WAF 403 on the documented-safe request shape). The corrected Simpleview guidance (Bloomington checklist, search-pattern doc, platforms doc) and ADR 0011 ride in this same implementation PR. Done when: the pending-feeds entry satisfies the DB trigger contract (scraper_cmd starts `python (scrapers|scripts)/`; output matches cities/<city>/<name>.ics); display name is exactly `Visit Bloomington` in the command, the pending comment, and every emitted X-SOURCE; no workflow, Node, browser, or dependency change; the aggregator list is unchanged and the source outranks Limestone Post with dual-credit primary-first; the checklist is implemented and documents the fallback trigger; add_scraper.py --test, make lint, and make test pass. Blocked by: items 1, 2, 4, 5, 6.

items.title: Review: code-review against spec #124 + triage via receiving-code-review
items.description: Invoke the code-review skill against the work completed in this branch, then triage every finding with the receiving-code-review skill IN THE SAME ITERATION. Fixed point: origin/main (three-dot diff origin/main...HEAD on the current feature branch). Standards axis: repo conventions (AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, ADRs) plus the skill's smell baseline. Spec axis: the original spec in issue #124. Report under ## Standards and ## Spec without merging the axes, ending with per-axis totals and the worst issue per axis. Do NOT fix code in this item; fixes happen in later loops under tdd and disciplined-engineering. After the report, triage each finding via receiving-code-review: worthwhile findings become new follow-up items appended to this prd.json -- one finding per item, each small and one-task shaped with reviewer-judgeable done criteria, each carrying title, description, passes:false, reference (the #124 spec line or the owning ticket), and priority 100, 110, 120... in dependency order (spec-correctness before standards-polish, dependencies first). Findings that are not worthwhile are NOT appended -- record them as a note on this item. Findings closable only by human acceptance (live deployed-calendar verification) are NEVER appended -- itemize them as deferred to the human_acceptance entry in notes instead; that entry sits outside the completion gate (it is not an items[] entry), so it never blocks COMPLETE and the loop must not attempt it. Never append a second review item; the review runs once. Done when: the two-axis report is in notes (every Spec finding quoting its #124 line, deferred-to-item-8 list included) AND all non-deferred worthwhile findings exist as appended follow-up items; then set passes:true on this item and stop. The loop continues onto the follow-ups by priority.
